lines.text: We plan to brake at six; video one's limiter allows ten. That gap is on purpose.
Plan more than the limiter allows, and the robot can't follow. It overshoots.
In our simulator, planning four with a limit of three overshot by sixty-seven centimeters.
Why not nine? In our simulator, that made tag line-ups less accurate. Six stayed accurate and quick.
Second, the finish line: under two centimeters, under two degrees, and under zero point zero five meters per second.
That's the measured speed. Asking to stop isn't the same as being stopped.
A waypoint finishes inside the switch radius, or five centimeters, whichever is bigger.
On our ninety degree corner: forty centimeters out, rolling at about one point five five.
